Install a functional Sandevistan in your operating-system slot at a Ripper Station. Press the operating-system ability key (V by default) to engage or disengage. Manual cancellation keeps the activation cost and recovery period.

Nearby hostile mobs move, think, attack and wind up more slowly. Fully recovered melee strikes can connect at your accelerated attack rate against affected mobs. Incoming arrows, tridents and supported thrown projectiles advance physically in smaller steps and still collide and inflict damage. Your own and other accelerated users' shots retain their speed.

Militech Experimental Sandevistan is a legendary-cache prototype inspired by David Martinez. It can also be fabricated after learning its design and obtaining the restricted parts. It offers intense acceleration with high strain and wear; no flight, teleportation, automatic critical hits or damage immunity.

Condition reduces efficiency and active duration. Every engagement causes wear and adds existing neurological instability. Repeated activations within the recovery window add further strain. Repair the implant at a Repair Station; a broken device cannot activate.

Dynalar is forgiving; Zetatech rewards airborne movement; Falcon sustains aggressive combat; Warp Dancer favors precision; Apogee combines strong acceleration with bounded kill rewards. At most six distinct hostile takedowns reward Falcon or Apogee, and active time cannot exceed 150% of its initial duration.

Time dilation is local. Other players keep normal controls; accelerated users cannot freeze one another. Overlapping fields use the strongest effect. World time, redstone and distant encounters continue normally. Bosses and encounter-specific projectiles are exempt.
Afterimages, edge pulses, FOV and sound volume have separate client presentation settings. Disabling them does not weaken the ability. Server balance and upgrade datapacks control gameplay.

Overload is a predictable danger of repeated unsafe use or severe damage, not a random first-use failure. It ends acceleration, damages the implant, inflicts a short physical aftershock and doubles recovery. Medical suppression does not erase usage history.

Cooldown reductions help set the recovery period when you engage, but subsequent refunds cannot erase the hardware recovery floor. Cancelling, changing dimensions, dying or reconnecting does not reset that recovery. Consecutive-use pressure gradually decays while you rest.
Act between your enemies' reactions. Speed, perception and neurological consequences.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skill_tree.s: The layout, skills, balance and progression rules are still to be decided and may change during development.
A look at what is planned beyond the current beta.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skill_tree.u: This tab is a preview placeholder. No skills or perks can be unlocked here in the current beta.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.fabr: The Schematics tab shows owned and missing designs. Missing designs use black silhouettes and encrypted names; their details cannot be opened. Learned designs show recipes and the original discovery history.
Choose a learned or public design, inspect its layout, then use Fill grid and Fabricate. Ingredients are consumed when assembly completes. Cancel leaves them intact; Clear grid returns them.
A full output bay pauses assembly. No fuel, redstone power or external energy supply is required.

Right-click a schematic to learn it permanently without consuming it. Locked recipes stay hidden from JEI, the Fabricator browser and wiki layouts. Learning also unlocks any other server recipes that require the same design.
Manufacture implants, chipware, modules and workshop components in a 5x5 assembly grid.
Basic Assembly supports tiers 1-2. Use a Precision Assembly Module on the block for tiers 3-4, then a High Spec Fabrication Module for tier 5. Make both modules in the Fabricator.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.recy: Recycle cyberware into up to three function-specific material types. Good, worn and heavily damaged implants have distinct, deterministic recovery bands.
Recycle limb modules into micro actuators.
Recycle consumables into wiring, paste or circuit plates by category.
The Recycler previews recovery from server recipes. Press Recycle 1 to dismantle one input and commit all recovered parts together.
Collect all recovered parts before the next operation. Closing returns inputs and completed recovery; a full inventory drops them safely.
Break down cyberware, modules, chipware and consumables into reusable parts.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.reli: This is a simplified example of overlapping sequences, not a complete high-tier puzzle. Start at top-row step 1 for 55.
Your second pick must stay in the same column, so move down to step 2 for BD, then across that row to step 3 for 4C.
At that point Daemon 1 is already cleared, because 55 BD 4C now appears in your path.
From step 3, move down the same column to FF, then across the last row to 0A. Those last two picks clear Daemon 2 as BD 4C FF and Daemon 3 as 4C FF 0A.
Daemon Chain
Example Route
Select tokens from the highlighted top row first, then alternate between the matching column and matching row.
A daemon is cleared once its full token sequence appears anywhere in the path you have built.
Clear every daemon before time or buffer runs out. Buffers hold 7/8/8/9 picks for Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary caches. Higher tiers require longer overlapping sequences.
Daemons do not grant separate effects or partial rewards. The cache opens only when every listed daemon is cleared.
Start by scanning the daemon sequences on the right and look for shared middle or ending tokens.
Because the path only has to contain the sequence, you can route one daemon into another instead of solving each one separately.
Selected cells are numbered on the grid, so you can review the full route directly while planning the next pick.
Hovered cells show whether the current line is legal. If a token is off the active row or column, it cannot be picked yet.
You can close the screen to deal with combat or reposition, then reopen the same cache and continue the same run if time remains.
Each placed Relic Cache keeps its own matrix and daemon list until that cache is opened.
Plan before selecting: the first pick starts the breach timer. Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary caches allow 50/40/32/25 seconds. Closing an executing breach does not pause it.
Caches can award intact equipment, service materials, schematic discoveries and specialized fabrication parts. Rewards depend on the server loot tables.
Uncommon caches replace one chest or barrel in igloo basements, jungle temples and pillager outposts.
Rare caches replace one chest or barrel in desert pyramids, woodland mansions and strongholds.
Epic caches replace one chest or barrel in trial chambers, ancient cities and bastion remnants.
Legendary caches replace one chest or barrel in end cities.
Bundled loot includes one primary reward, one or two support rolls and one fabrication-discovery roll. Server datapacks can change these pools.

Placement also checks older loaded structures, but only untouched loot-table chests or barrels. Opened containers, player storage and double chests are preserved. Each supported structure receives at most one generated cache.

Ask a Fixer or Netrunner about nearby relic caches to receive coordinates and a tuned compass for the nearest known cache you have not breached. No compass is required beforehand; it is removed when you click its cache. They do not reveal unexplored terrain. The Relic Scanner highlights every cache tier and prioritizes caches over ordinary containers within scan range.
Tiered breach caches placed into high-value structures.
Relic Caches
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.ripp: Inspect passive effects, active implants, upgrade level and integrity.
Manage chipware and modules when the selected implant supports them.
Open the archive directly from the station UI.
The Ripper Station is the main body-management screen.
It exposes body slots, current installed hardware, chrome totals and slot-by-slot planning.
Install, compare and manage cyberware, chipware and modules.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.tech: Review current integrity, the full-repair result and exact required quantities before paying.
Increase service tier unlocks higher implant tiers for this service. Personal progression remains when the machine is replaced.
Repairs restore full integrity while keeping installed chips, modules, upgrade levels and custom names.
The Repair Station restores existing implants. Upgrade levels are applied at the separate Upgrade Station.
Repair uses up to two server-defined materials. Quantities scale with missing integrity; one operation restores the item fully.
Preview the required parts, fill materials from your inventory, then press Repair.
Restore damaged cyberware while retaining upgrades and custom data.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.upgr: Increase service tier unlocks higher implant tiers for your character. Repair, Upgrade and Recycler progression are separate and survive replacing a machine.
Upgrading preserves current integrity, name, installed chips, modules and other item data. It never grants a repair.
Each step uses its server datapack price and adds exactly one level. The item page shows the current track, level cap and numerical benefits.
The Upgrade Station never changes the model or manufactured tier. Model conversions use an explicit Fabricator recipe and its schematic requirements.

Insert an uninstalled implant, review the exact benefits and up to two material types, then Fill materials and Upgrade +1. The preview cannot be collected; the completed item appears in its separate output slot.
Improve the same physical implant through its server-defined +1 track.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.bleed: Damage taken per stack during active aggression: +%s
This status is meant to read as active bleeding under exertion.
Moving while bleeding increases the periodic damage.
Periodic behavior: bleed damage over time.
Visual identity: crimson dust and directional trailing spray while moving.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.corro: This status is meant to read as chemical breakdown.
Periodic behavior: steady corrosion damage over time.
Visual identity: toxic yellow-green dust, runoff and corrosive drip lines.
This status is meant to read as a deliberate tracking lock, not an enchantment reuse.
Periodic behavior: target outline highlighting for follow-up attacks.
Visual identity: cyan-green targeting rings plus the shared outline renderer.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.overh: This status is meant to read as internal thermal overload.
Moving while overheated increases the periodic damage.
Periodic behavior: keeps the target burning and deals fire-style damage pulses.
Visual identity: flame, ember dust, smoke plumes and heat rings.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.shock: This status is meant to read as electrical seizure, not a generic potion effect.
Periodic behavior: electrical jitter, movement disruption and outline highlighting.
Visual identity: cyan-white sparks, electric dust and violent body jitter.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.traum: This status is meant to read as blunt internal damage.
Periodic behavior: dampens movement and makes displacement worse.
Visual identity: red impact dust, damage bursts and heavy shock pulses.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.cyber: Higher cyberstrain applies passive penalties to movement, attack speed, healing, ability cooldowns and max health.
Suppression medicine temporarily reduces effective cyberstrain.
Frontal cortex hardware can add extra cyberstrain on top of installed chrome.
Use lower-cost implants for early builds.
Use suppressants when pushing into high-strain setups.
Treat active cyberware and stimulant use as part of the risk budget, not just the installed load.
The pressure system that limits how much chrome a body can run safely.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.progr: Cyberware, chipware, limb modules and advanced parts are manufactured in the Fabricator. Basic supplies, consumables and machine blocks also use crafting-table recipes.
Public designs are available immediately. Schematic-locked recipes remain hidden and unusable until learned, including in JEI and the Fabricator.
Fabricator capability controls supported tiers. Repair, Upgrade and Recycler service tiers are separate personal unlocks.
Relic Cache world generation is live. Each supported structure replaces one chest or barrel with a tiered cache block.
Uncommon: igloo basement, jungle temple, pillager outpost. Rare: desert pyramid, woodland mansion, stronghold.
Epic: trial chambers, ancient city, bastion remnant. Legendary: end city.
Techies, Netrunners and Mercs issue six kinds of contracts. Dialogue and the quest archive track the current objective and return to the issuer.
Rewards include eurodollars, trust and supplies, with a chance for schematic or part discoveries. High-tier jobs can reach restricted designs.
Item pages use current server recipes and service definitions. Cache loot is controlled by server tables; the cache preview is a sample of possible rewards, not a promise of drops.
A model conversion is a Fabricator recipe. A +1 improvement preserves the same model; repair only restores integrity.
The live acquisition split and implemented world sources.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.psych: Immunoblockers and Chrome Suppressant reduce instability and can shorten an active episode.
After an episode ends, Aftershock remains briefly and keeps some penalties active.
High-strain crisis behavior driven by effective cyberstrain plus instability.
Major episodes prioritize players first, hostile mobs second and untamed land animals last.
Ignored targets include configured nuisance types such as bats, fish, silverfish and endermites.
Minor episode: aggressive surge with boosted combat stats and control pressure, but not the full major takeover.
Major episode: full hostile autopilot, target pursuit, top-screen server tracker and major penalty package.
Cyberpsychosis does not trigger from installed chrome alone. It requires psychosis-risk cyberstrain plus accumulated instability.
Instability builds from combat, cyberware activations, certain consumables and staying in the danger bands.
